title: Home Purchase Agreement — Buyer Delay in Closing
content:
**Clause 12. Buyer delay in closing.**

12.1 This clause applies when the buyer does not close on the scheduled closing date of a Home Purchase Agreement for a reason on the buyer's side.

12.2 *Retired accrual clause.* The former clause under which a closing delay per diem of the collection's per diem rate per calendar day accrues from the day after the collection's per diem grace days have elapsed, booked as one charge per delay period with its first and last day (under which the per diem days were the buyer delay days less the grace days, never below zero, and the charge was the per diem days times the per diem rate) is **no longer in force**. The closing delay per diem is figured and booked under the current basis that superseded it.

12.3 *Default notice.* Once the buyer delay days exceed the collection's buyer delay figure, Calloway sends a default notice under the agreement's buyer default and termination terms.

12.4 *Buyer delay days.* The buyer delay days are the calendar days elapsed after the scheduled closing date, counted from the day after the scheduled closing date through the current date, on an agreement still in status closing scheduled.

**Notes to Clause 12.**

(a) "Exceed" is strict. In a collection whose buyer delay figure is 30, 30 days of buyer delay do not exceed it; 31 days do.

(b) *Hypothetical illustration.* An agreement in a collection with a 45-day figure has a scheduled closing date of 1 March and is still closing scheduled. Through 15 April the buyer delay days are 45, not exceeding the figure; on 16 April they are 46 and exceed it, so the default notice is sent under the default and termination terms.

(c) An agreement that has moved out of closing scheduled, for example to closed, no longer accumulates buyer delay days under 12.4.

superseded_clauses: a closing_delay_per_diem of per_diem_usd per calendar day accrues from the day after per_diem_grace_days have elapsed, booked as one charge per delay period with its first and last day
